PullRequest.Title: test(unit): migrate the browser test runner and the reporters to TypeScript
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

## Why

This is the second step of moving the unit test runners to TypeScript one at a time, after the node.js runner in #349820. The browser runner now gets the same type check.

## What changed

- `test/unit/browser/index.js` is now `index.ts`, an ES module like the node.js runner (`test/unit/browser/package.json` sets `"type": "module"`). `test/unit/tsconfig.json` checks it too.
- `test/unit/reporter.js` and `fullJsonStreamReporter.js` are now `.mts` files, ES modules whatever the package type says. The browser runner imports their typed exports, and the Electron runner, which is still CommonJS, requires `reporter.mts`. `createRequire` keeps loading mocha's reporters and a custom `--reporter` with CommonJS resolution. The `full-json-stream` reporter no longer writes `currentRetry`: mocha keeps it private, even in mocha 12, and nothing reads it.
- `allowJs` and `maxNodeModuleJsDepth` give TypeScript the types of `yaserver`, `mocha-junit-reporter` and `mocha/lib/stats-collector`, which have no `@types` packages. `index.ts` casts `mocha-junit-reporter` to a constructor, because its JSDoc does not mark it as one.
- `parallel.ts` exports with `module.exports`, which TypeScript does not read, so `index.ts` repeats the signatures that it calls (`IParallel`), as the node.js runner does.
- The import rules of `test/unit` allow `@playwright/*` and `mocha/lib/**`, as they do for `test/automation`.
- `package.json`, `pr-win32-test.yml`, the selfhost test provider, the `detectChanges` build test and two comments point to `index.ts`.
- Two earlier commits delete what nothing reads: the minimist `describe` option, the Playwright `devtools` launch option (Playwright 1.61 ignores it), and the allowlist entry for `test/unit/node/index.js` that #349820 left behind.

## Scope

`renderer.html` and the other shared helpers (`parallel.ts`, `coverage.js`) are unchanged. The Electron runner only requires `reporter.mts` instead of `reporter.js`.

## Tradeoffs

Two runners now repeat the `IParallel` signatures. Both copies go away when `parallel.ts` moves to ESM exports, after the Electron runner. The types that TypeScript reads from the JavaScript of `yaserver`, `mocha-junit-reporter` and `mocha/lib/stats-collector` are mostly `any`, so the check does not verify the arguments of those calls. Declaration files would check them, at the cost of maintaining hand-written types in this repository.

## Blast Radius

`pnpm run test-browser`, `pnpm run test-browser-no-install`, every CI job that runs the browser unit tests, and browser runs from the selfhost test provider. Through `reporter.mts`, also how the Electron runner applies `--reporter`. Because this changes a test runner, ripple runs every unit test on this PR.

## Verification

- `pnpm run typecheck-test-unit`: passes.
- The runner before and after, for 13 scenarios in chromium and webkit: identical exit codes, test counts, rerun and flaky-test messages, and JUnit output. The table is in a comment below.
- Both runners before and after the reporter commits, for the default, `dot`, `full-json-stream` (also with a failing test) and `json-stream --reporter-options a=b` reporters and a missing one: identical output, with durations and process IDs removed, except the dropped `currentRetry`.
- `hygiene` and `oxlint` with `--changed-since` the base, and the `detectChanges` build test that reads the runner's `excludeGlob`: pass. `ripple plan` for the branch, and for a change to a module that the runners load: passes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run browser unit tests locally, in CI, or through the selfhost test provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Load the runner and dependencies, discover selected test files, create the HTTP server, launch a browser/context/page, discover and compress CSS paths, load renderer.html and test modules, run tests, and close the browser. Selfhost additionally starts one runner subprocess and consumes its stdout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the browser test runner using process.execPath.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runner process per selfhost invocation, not one per selected test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same spawn executed browser/index.js; it now executes browser/index.ts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runner startup precedes test discovery and execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load runner dependencies, read an optional run list, glob test and CSS files, and optionally read nls.messages.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Module loads once per process; one test discovery per process, one CSS glob per browser attempt, and one NLS read per built-output browser attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The JavaScript runner performed the same dependency loads, discovery, CSS compression, and optional NLS read. TypeScript adds bounded native type-stripping work for the migrated files, without multiplying these operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery and page setup must finish before tests run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the requested Playwright browser and close it after the attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser launch per requested browser attempt in single-process mode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same browser/context/page lifecycle existed; only the unused devtools launch option is removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Browser launch and page initialization precede execution; close is awaited before completing the attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve renderer resources and compiled modules over localhost HTTP.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Requests scale with distinct modules and resources loaded in each fresh page; shared imports are reused by that page's module loader.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same static server and sequential test-module import loop served the same selected modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resource loading is on test startup's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer test options and events, console arguments, and optional isolation findings between browser and runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One loadAndRun request per attempt, events proportional to T, console transfers proportional to emitted messages, and one optional isolation collection per attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls and payload construction existed; added interfaces and casts do not add serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Execution and reporting depend on these existing browser bindings; console listeners are awaited during cleanup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform test-requested read/write/readdir/unlink/mkdir operations and optionally append isolation findings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One filesystem operation per explicit test RPC; one report append per attempt with nonempty optional findings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same HTTP RPC dispatch, filesystem operations, and report append were present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Test RPCs block their callers; optional findings are collected after execution and before attempt cleanup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N selected browser-compatible test files and their shared dependency graph, C CSS files, T test/hook events, and filesystem requests explicitly made by tests. --runList entries are normalized and deduplicated in a Set before file filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Without workers, requested browsers run concurrently unless --sequential is set; module imports within each page are sequential. Individual test filesystem requests follow test scheduling. The diff preserves these policies and the default browser list.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Node dependencies remain cached per runner process; browser modules are cached per page. Fresh browser contexts do not share an application module cache across attempts. OS/package caches can reduce cold filesystem and installation costs. No cache invalidation, negative caching, or request coalescing changes were found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from complete runner diff and traced selfhost, renderer, and cleanup paths that expensive operation counts and scheduling are preserved.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native TypeScript/ESM startup overhead was not measured. No changed scaling mechanism establishes an actionable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: entry-point and typing changes preserve discovery, browser launch count, event traffic, and lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run selected browser tests in parallel workers and rerun failures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Discover modules, calculate the capped worker count, spawn workers, load modules in every worker page, claim and execute files, collect worker reports, then optionally rerun unresolved failures in fresh single browsers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn runner workers, each of which launches a browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: W runner children and W browser launches per browser's first attempt, plus at most R single-browser rerun launches; no worker fan-out on reruns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical worker caps, arguments, spawning, and rerun placement; __filename becomes import.meta.filename.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First-attempt completion waits for all workers; retries follow report aggregation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load test modules and issue synchronous localhost file-claim RPCs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All N files load in each worker page. Up to approximately W*N normal claim attempts, plus per-worker start and successful-file recordRun calls; failure retries are capped at three per RPC. Claims operate per file, not per test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderer helper, import loop, claim scheduling, and retries were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Imports precede execution; synchronous claim calls gate selection of subsequent suites.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Atomically create claim directories, record run order and worker reports, read aggregated reports, and remove temporary worker storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Claim filesystem attempts follow RPC cardinality after ownership caching; reports occur once per worker; cleanup once per worker group.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: parallel.ts is unchanged, including caches, filesystem operations, and cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Claims gate work allocation; report reads and cleanup precede aggregate completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N selected files, W capped workers, B requested browsers, and R configured retries. W is limited by requested count, CPUs, and one worker per 2 GB; with --runList it is additionally limited by file count and the existing 75-files-per-worker policy.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most W worker processes for one browser at a time; browsers serialize when workers apply. Only the first attempt uses workers. Reruns run sequentially in one browser per browser type. CI requests four workers, subject to existing caps.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each worker has its own Node/page module caches and loads all N selected files. File claims cache successful ownership, claimAll caches its boolean result, and recorded-file Sets suppress duplicate log entries. Failed ownership claims are not negatively cached, unchanged. HTTP claim requests retry at most three times on failure.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: worker policy, shared helper implementation, page RPCs, and rerun call paths were inspected and compared with the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The existing W*N module loading and claim overhead can be substantial, but this PR does not introduce or amplify it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the migration preserves effective concurrency, file-level ownership, and single-browser retries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stream test results to selfhost consumers or produce console/JUnit reports in browser and Electron runners
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Load reporter modules, construct reporters for each runner attempt, serialize relevant test events, and write output. Electron waits for reporter drain before treating its renderer as done.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify each emitted JSON-stream event, including failure and coverage payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialization per emitted event; failure construction adds one small intermediate clean(test) object but does not copy the potentially large actual/expected payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reporter serialized the same event families and failure payloads. currentRetry is now omitted; failure fields are assembled using object spread rather than assignment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous work occurs during reporting, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write JSON lines to stdout for the selfhost output scanner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stdout write per emitted event, unchanged; the write callback now resolves through a wrapper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stream writes and lastEvent-based drain existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Electron explicitly awaits drain on completion; live selfhost results arrive through the pipe.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/load reporter modules and write optional JUnit output via mocha-junit-reporter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reporter module loads are cached per process; JUnit files remain separated per browser, worker, and attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reporters were eagerly loaded, resolved, and constructed. Electron now requires reporter.mts instead of reporter.js.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reporter setup precedes events; report output is part of completing the test attempt.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: T test events, F failures with their existing diagnostic payloads, optional coverage events, and one reporter set per attempt/worker.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Event callbacks perform synchronous JSON construction/stringification and issue stdout writes; there is no newly introduced batching, queue, or parallel reporter creation. JUnit and console reporters are paired in the existing --tfs path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reporter modules are loaded once per process through normal module caching. Built-in and custom reporter resolution still use createRequire with CommonJS resolution. No per-event imports or new retained history are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from both reporter diffs, browser reporter construction, Electron drain handling, and selfhost launch arguments.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No throughput measurement was performed; the added failure-only object spread and callback wrapper do not establish a meaningful performance degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: event cardinality, large-payload handling, stream lifetime, and reporter resolution are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collect diagnostics after a browser test run stalls
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Only after the existing inactivity watchdog fires: probe page responsiveness with a ten-second timeout, enumerate processes, optionally sample browser processes on macOS, then exit with failure.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One probe per watchdog-triggered diagnostic run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same timed probe preceded process collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Failure exit waits for the response or the existing ten-second timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run ps on non-Windows platforms and sample each matching browser process on macOS.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ps process; on macOS, P concurrent sample processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same execFile calls, Promise.all placement, and timeouts existed. Converting pid to String makes the existing sample command arguments valid and can enable intended diagnostic work that previously failed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Diagnostics finish before failure exit, off the successful test path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the diagnostic output directory and write native samples through the sample subprocess.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One recursive mkdir and up to P sample files per macOS diagnostic run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same output directory, filenames, and intended sampling operations existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only delays an already-stalled run's diagnostic failure exit.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P matching browser processes and total system process count for the ps snapshot; this is a failure-only path, not normal test startup or execution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One diagnostic run per fired watchdog. macOS samples matching P processes concurrently with Promise.all, each with a 180-second subprocess timeout; unchanged scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No diagnostic cache; each stall takes one fresh process snapshot. The watchdog interval is cleared before diagnostics and disposed after normal execution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in diagnostic-only reachability, one-shot watchdog behavior, and preserved process-count scaling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Successful sampling may take longer than previously invalid arguments; duration and matching process count are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the only substantive change repairs intended, bounded failure diagnostics rather than adding work to an important successful path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type-check test infrastructure and select affected CI tests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing typecheck-test-unit command now checks browser and reporter sources as well as node runner sources. Ripple reads the runner patterns and dependency references before selecting test jobs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the additionally included TypeScript modules and JavaScript dependency sources for type inference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per source in the compiler program, with node_modules JavaScript traversal limited to depth one rather than per test execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The compiler program included node/**/*.ts only and did not opt into JavaScript source inference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds expected checking work to the infrastructure type-check step, not browser test runtime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recognize .mts runner sources when building the existing test dependency model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two renamed reporter files join the runner-pattern matches; they replace previously matched .js reporters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reporter sources matched test/unit/**/*.js, and test/unit/** was already covered by runEverything.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The newly included browser runner and two reporter modules, their bounded directly followed JavaScript dependency surface with maxNodeModuleJsDepth=1, and repository graph size for the existing planner.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new subprocess loop, worker count, or CI job fan-out is introduced by the changed configuration. Type checking remains one tsc invocation; planning remains the existing planner invocation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The unit tsconfig has noEmit and skipLibCheck and introduces no custom cache. Ripple's existing cached binary and test-selection behavior are unchanged; renamed .mts reporters are now covered by the runner patterns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that compiler inclusion expands intentionally and runner-pattern coverage preserves the renamed files' dependency role.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Additional typecheck time is unmeasured; no unbounded traversal, repeated compiler invocation, or unintended test-selection expansion was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added bounded checking is the migration's intended behavior and the planner update preserves existing coverage.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 16 changed files and all browser-runner diff pages. Traced startup/execution, worker allocation and reruns, browser/Electron reporting and selfhost consumption, failure diagnostics, type checking, and CI planning. No high-confidence diff-introduced actionable performance regressions or qualifying performance-regression fixes were found. Static read-only review; no profiling or runtime execution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
